hook.text: Send spam from your server and it lands on a blocklist. Now every email you send gets rejected.

buildup.text: DNS-based blocklists (DNSBLs) track IPs known to send spam. Receivers query them in real time.

discovery.text: Spamhaus, Barracuda, and SpamCop maintain major lists. One listing can block your mail worldwide.

twist.text: Shared hosting means shared IPs. One spammy neighbor can get your innocent server blocklisted too.

climax.text: Reputation is rebuilt slowly: clean sending, low bounce rates, and proper authentication. Days to weeks.

punchline.text: IP reputation is email currency. Lose it and delivery stops.

quiz.question: What is a DNSBL?
options: A DNS-based list of IPs known to send spam
A tool for compressing email attachments

details.summary: Email blocklists are databases of IP addresses and domains known for sending spam. Major blocklists like Spamhaus, Barracuda, and SORBS are queried by receiving servers in real time to reject mail from listed senders. Getting listed can immediately stop all email delivery from an organization.
details.whyItMatters: Being listed on a major blocklist effectively silences your email communications. Understanding how blocklists work is critical for maintaining email delivery capability.
takeaways: Blocklists track IPs and domains associated with spam
Receiving servers query blocklists in real time during delivery
Getting listed requires a delisting request and remediation

faq.question: How does an organization end up on a blocklist?
faq.answer: Sending spam, having compromised accounts that send spam, hitting spam traps, or generating excessive bounces can trigger listing. Shared IP addresses mean one bad sender can get the entire IP listed. Sudden sending volume increases also raise flags with blocklist operators.

faq.question: How do you get removed from a blocklist?
faq.answer: Identify and fix the cause of listing first. Most blocklists have a delisting request process. Some automatically delist after a cooling period if no further spam is detected. Spamhaus, the most influential blocklist, requires direct communication and evidence of remediation.
